Request for Proposal (RFP)
Design, Development and Deployment of a Digital Case Management Platform for the Regional
Public Health Directorate
RFP Reference: RPHD/IT/2026-014
1. Introduction and Background
The Regional Public Health Directorate (RPHD) is seeking proposals from qualified firms to design,
develop, and deploy a Digital Case Management Platform (“the Platform”) to replace its current
paper-based and spreadsheet-based case tracking processes across 12 regional health centers. The
Platform must support case intake, triage, referral tracking, reporting to the national health information
system, and role-based access for over 300 field agents and administrative staff.
2. Scope of Work
The selected firm will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of the Platform, including requirements
gathering workshops with RPHD staff, system architecture and data model design, development of a
secure web application and companion mobile app for field agents, integration with the existing National
Health Information Exchange (NHIE) API, data migration from the legacy spreadsheet system, user
acceptance testing, staff training, and a 12-month post-launch support and maintenance period.
2.1 Expected Deliverables
l
Requirements and functional specification document, validated by RPHD stakeholders
l
System architecture and data model documentation
l
Web-based case management application with role-based access control (Admin, Regional Supervisor,
Field Agent)
l
Companion mobile application (Android and iOS) for offline-capable field data entry
l
Integration module connecting to the National Health Information Exchange (NHIE) API
l
Data migration of existing case records from the legacy spreadsheet system
l
User acceptance testing (UAT) report and sign-off
l
Training materials and delivery of training sessions for 300+ staff across 12 health centers
l
Deployment to RPHD's production environment
l
12 months of post-launch technical support and maintenance3. Timeline and Key Dates

4. Indicative Budget
The total available budget for this engagement, inclusive of development, integration, training, and the
12-month support period, is USD 380,000. Proposals exceeding this ceiling by more than 10% may be
disqualified at the evaluation committee's discretion. Firms are asked to provide a itemized cost
breakdown by deliverable and by project phase.
5. Evaluation Criteria
Proposals will be evaluated using the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method, with a 75%
weighting on technical quality and 25% weighting on financial proposal. The technical evaluation will score
proposals against the following criteria:
CriterionWeight
Relevant experience with similar public-sector case management systems25%
Proposed technical approach and architecture20%
Qualifications and experience of proposed key personnel20%
Implementation and training plan15%
Data security and privacy compliance approach15%
Local presence / ability to provide on-site support5%6. Eligibility Requirements
l
Minimum 5 years of experience delivering software solutions in healthcare, public health, or a related
regulated sector
l
At least 2 reference projects of comparable scope completed in the last 5 years
l
Demonstrated experience integrating with government or national health information exchange APIs
l
Proposed team must include a Project Manager, Solutions Architect, at least 2 Full-Stack Developers, a
Mobile Developer, a QA/Test Lead, and a Data Privacy/Security Specialist
l
Valid business registration and tax compliance certificate in the country of operation
7. Data Privacy and Security Requirements
Given the sensitive nature of patient case data, the Platform must comply with the national Health Data
Protection Act (2022) and implement encryption at rest and in transit, role-based access control, full audit
logging, and a documented data retention and deletion policy. The selected firm must be willing to sign a
Data Processing Agreement prior to contract execution and submit to a third-party security audit before
go-live.
8. Submission Instructions
Proposals must be submitted electronically in PDF format to procurement@rphd-gov.example no later
than 31 August 2026, 17:00 local time. Late submissions will not be considered. Each proposal must
include: (a) a technical proposal not exceeding 25 pages, (b) CVs of all proposed key personnel, (c) at
least 2 reference letters or contactable references from similar past projects, and (d) a separate sealed
financial proposal.
9. Contact and Clarifications
All clarification questions must be submitted in writing to procurement@rphd-gov.example by 10 August
2026. Answers will be circulated to all firms that have registered interest, without disclosing the identity of
the requesting firm.
